content.text:
I think only **mp-1105158 (Sr₂ScGaO₅)** is present.

1. **Single-phase fits.** I fitted each of the nine candidates alone. Sr₂ScGaO₅ was the only one that fitted the pattern meaningfully, with an R-factor of 0.66 at 0 % strain. The other eight all scored about 0.98 to 1.0 and left the main observed peaks (about 29.3°, 30.5° and 31.7°, the strongest) almost untouched.
2. **Sr₂ScGaO₅ residual.** What's left after this fit is mostly dip–peak–dip patterns sitting on the observed peaks. The largest is at 31.7° (about −20 / +25 / −19). That looks like a peak-shape or position mismatch with the same phase, not extra peaks from a new one.
3. **No clear second phase.** The only other leftovers are weak bumps near 23°, 24.6° and 39°, about 2 to 6 on the 100 scale. None of the other eight candidates fitted the pattern on its own.

The weak spot: I did not run two-phase fits (Sr₂ScGaO₅ plus each other candidate). So a minor second phase is unlikely but not ruled out, and an R-factor of 0.66 is still poor.
